review_title: Defective Products, Terrible Quality Control & One of the Worst Return Experiences I've Ever Had!!
review_text:
I have spent over 10 hours, sent more than 50 emails, and travelled to six different return locations trying to return products that should never have been shipped in the first place.

The reason for my return wasn't that I changed my mind.
The clothing arrived with incorrect sizing, poor workmanship, unfinished construction, and obvious quality issues. Some items looked like they had never been properly finished before being packaged. The sizing was nowhere close to what was advertised, making several items completely unwearable. These are quality control failures that fall entirely on SHEIN.
Instead of standing behind the products they sell, SHEIN leaves customers to deal with the consequences.

The customer service has been just as disappointing as the products. After more than 50 emails, I continue receiving the same generic copy-and-paste responses that completely ignore the concerns I've raised. Not once has anyone meaningfully addressed the poor quality of the items, the incorrect sizing, or the countless hours I've spent trying to return them.
The biggest issue has been SHEIN's return process in Toronto.

I previously completed a SHEIN return while I was in Vancouver, where the return was handled through Canada Post. It was simple, professional, and took only a few minutes. That's exactly how a return process should work.My experience in Toronto has been the complete opposite.

SHEIN uses a third-party return network that has been an absolute nightmare. I have been sent from location to location, only to find businesses that were closed, difficult to access, or operating with extremely limited hours. One designated return location had nothing more than a handwritten piece of paper taped to the door listing its business hours. I took photographs because I couldn't believe a company the size of SHEIN expects customers to rely on a return network operating like this.
I work full-time and don't permanently live in Toronto. Spending days travelling across the city trying to return defective clothing is completely unreasonable. I've documented every trip, every location, walking directions, screenshots, emails, and photographs because I simply couldn't believe how difficult this process became.

No customer should have to spend weeks chasing down return locations because a company shipped merchandise that failed basic quality standards.

The most frustrating part is the complete lack of accountability. Instead of acknowledging the problems or offering a practical solution, SHEIN continues sending automated responses while the customer absorbs all of the time, inconvenience, and expense.

A return policy is supposed to protect customers when products arrive defective or not as described. It should not become a second job.

If SHEIN can provide a simple, efficient return process through Canada Post in one Canadian city, there is no reason customers in another city should be forced through such a disorganized and inaccessible third-party network.

This entire experience has shown me that once something goes wrong, customer service and accountability disappear. I expected far better from a global retailer.

I sincerely hope SHEIN reviews both its quality control and its Canadian return process because no customer should have to fight this hard to return products that should never have passed inspection in the first place.
I will not be shopping with SHEIN again, and I cannot recommend them based on this experience.

review_title: Finger weg von SHEIN – Retoure nachweislich zugestellt, 875,96 € seit knapp 2 Monaten offen
review_text:
Ich laufe mittlerweile seit über zwei Monaten meiner Rückerstattung in Höhe von 875,96 € hinterher. Und nein – hier geht es nicht um ein paar Euro, sondern um eine sehr hohe Summe, auf die man als normaler Mensch angewiesen ist.

Es handelte sich um eine kombinierte Rücksendung, weil SHEIN selbst empfiehlt, mehrere Rücksendungen zusammenzufassen, um Versandkosten zu sparen. Genau das habe ich getan.

Ich habe meine Rücksendung ordnungsgemäß bei DHL abgegeben. Ich besitze den offiziellen Einlieferungsbeleg und die Sendungsverfolgung, aus der eindeutig hervorgeht, dass das Paket im Lager angekommen ist – inklusive Datum, Uhrzeit und Zustellung.

Trotzdem behauptet SHEIN seit Wochen immer wieder, die Retoure sei angeblich nicht im Lager eingetroffen. Egal welche Nachweise ich einreiche – ich bekomme jedes Mal dieselben Standardantworten. Niemand geht auf meinen konkreten Fall ein.

Nachdem ich angekündigt habe, rechtliche Schritte einzuleiten, verlangt SHEIN plötzlich Dinge wie Videomaterial vom Verpacken oder Einliefern der Retoure. Welcher normale Mensch filmt sich bitte dabei, wie er ein Paket verpackt oder zur DHL bringt? Außerdem soll ich einen Nachweis über das Paketgewicht liefern. Wie soll ich als Kunde an interne Gewichtsangaben kommen? Ich habe darauf überhaupt keinen Zugriff. Ich habe sogar mehrfach bei DHL angerufen. Selbst dort konnte man nicht nachvollziehen, warum trotz aller Nachweise immer weitere Forderungen gestellt werden.

Seit über zwei Monaten verbringe ich einen Großteil meiner Freizeit damit, E-Mails zu schreiben, zu telefonieren und immer wieder dieselben Unterlagen einzureichen. Es kostet unheimlich viel Zeit, Kraft und Nerven. Ich habe wirklich noch nie in meinem Leben einen derart frustrierenden Kundenservice erlebt.

Am Telefon fühlt sich niemand zuständig und per E-Mail erhält man immer wieder dieselben Standardtexte. Man hat das Gefühl, mit einer Wand zu sprechen.

Meine Verantwortung war es, das Paket ordnungsgemäß bei DHL abzugeben. Das habe ich getan. Ich kann nachweisen, dass es an der auf dem Retourenschein angegebenen Adresse zugestellt wurde. Was danach innerhalb des Unternehmens passiert, liegt nicht mehr in meiner Verantwortung.

Da ich auf normalem Weg nicht weiterkomme, habe ich inzwischen die Verbraucherzentrale informiert und einen Anwalt beauftragt, meine Ansprüche durchzusetzen. Ich werde den Fall notfalls gerichtlich klären lassen.

Diese Erfahrung hat mich psychisch enorm belastet. Niemand sollte wochenlang einer berechtigten Rückerstattung hinterherlaufen müssen, obwohl alle erforderlichen Nachweise vorliegen.

Für mich steht fest: Nie wieder SHEIN. Ich werde dort nie wieder bestellen und auch meiner Familie, meinen Freunden und meinem Bekanntenkreis davon abraten. Diese Erfahrung hat inzwischen jeder in meinem Umfeld mitbekommen und viele haben dadurch selbst Angst, dort zu bestellen. So sollte kein Unternehmen mit seinen Kunden umgehen.

Ich hoffe, dass meine Erfahrung andere Menschen davor bewahrt, dieselbe Situation erleben zu müssen.

Therefore, if SHEIN decided to refund the original card, they should have refunded the exact amount corresponding to the original card transaction, not several fragmented amounts. Because of this, my bank is not properly recognizing or releasing part of the refund, since the amounts do not match the original purchase transaction.

This makes the situation even more frustrating. Why ask me where I wanted the refund to be sent if, in the end, they were going to process it however they wanted, without following the refund method I provided?

As a result, after almost a month of emails, claims, and additional paperwork with my bank, I still cannot access a significant part of my money.

This has been a very frustrating and poorly managed refund process. SHEIN should have respected the refund method I requested, or at least processed the refund correctly according to the original transaction.

Unfortunately, based on this experience, I cannot recommend SHEIN’s customer service or refund process.

review_title: Negative 5 or an ‘F’ grade for their app
review_text:
First off, let me start by saying that I’m making a review on the experience I’ve had with the app and the experience that I’ve had with shopping on temu.com
I’m rating the Temu app with a NEGATIVE 5 based on its EXTREME persistence to push you to buy with the spinning wheels and flash fast messages no matter how many times you try closing the “game” windows. Every time you hit to close out ANOTHER game window pops up insisting that you “spin the wheel”. The other thing that is concerning is the excessive texts you receive from them, especially the ones stating that because you’re such a great customer and they’re “feeling generous” they are “reimbursing your purchase”. To be clear, the definition of reimbursement means ‘to return monies [you’ve spent] on a purchase’. I fell for that trap thinking I was actually receiving money back from Temu because the price on an item I bought had dropped between the time I purchased the item/s and the time it shipped. No! I followed the prompts guiding me to “choose an item” to qualify for said reimbursement and hit checkout only to find that there is no reimbursement but that I was charged FULL PRICE for the items I was supposed to get said reimbursement on!!! I had to then go through the process of requesting a refund for what they charged to my account!! This happened day before yesterday.
I did some research on Temu and their horrible performance and will take the suggestion of someone else who was taken in by their ploys and delete my account and block them from texting me. IF I feel to buy more of what I previously bought I’ll only shop through my private browser, using an entirely separate account and private phone number.
Next, my purchases: I have bought women’s pjs, pants, sneakers and rechargeable lights, a tiny air cooler fan system with a water misting capability, a cat toy and some other small things that I’m truly happy with. But I *have* found MANY sellers that have padded their items with fake or several times reposted “customer” reviews to try fooling you into thinking the item is a 5 star perfect purchase. review_text: I used to be a regular customer, but after my recent experiences with Temu, I strongly advise everyone to be extremely cautious. Temu heavily advertises their "Local Warehouse" delivery as a major feature, but in reality, you pay the exact same price (or sometimes higher) as you would on major marketplaces like Amazon. The difference is that Amazon delivers the item the same day or next day, while Temu's "local" package takes weeks to arrive from halfway across the country, completely missing their guaranteed delivery windows. On top of that, most items are extremely low quality—what looks decent in pictures turns out to be cheap trash. The app is also filled with predatory and manipulative games like Farmland and Fishland designed to waste your time and trick you into buying useless items. When a package is delayed past the contract deadline or misdelivered, customer service becomes a complete nightmare. I spent 3.5 hours in support chats being repeatedly gaslighted. They accept invalid "proof of delivery" photos (like a package sitting on a driver's lap in their vehicle or generic photos without unit numbers) while demanding buyers file police reports for minor missing items. Even when you explicitly cancel an order due to a breach of delivery terms, they ignore you, force the late package onto your doorstep, and refuse a proper refund. To make matters worse, instead of returning funds to the original payment card they unlawfully dump it into Temu Credits to trap your money in their ecosystem. I have had to file formal claims with the Better Business Bureau (BBB) and initiate bank disputes to get my money back. Temu lies even in their official responses to regulators, claiming "no record of cancellation" despite hours of documented chat history. Avoid this platform—the savings are fake, the logistics are unreliable, and the customer service is predatory.

review_title: 3ᵉ avis – Toujours ni colis, ni remboursement de 351,77 €
review_text:
C’est malheureusement mon 3ᵉ avis, car malgré plusieurs semaines de démarches, je suis toujours sans solution.

J’ai commandé un processeur informatique sur AliExpress (commande n° 3074718559707335) pour un montant de 351,77 €.

Le suivi indique que le colis aurait été déposé dans ma boîte aux lettres. Pourtant, je n’ai jamais reçu cette commande.

J’ai immédiatement vérifié auprès de mes voisins, du gardien de ma résidence et de La Poste : personne n’a récupéré mon colis. La Poste m’a confirmé qu’aucune photo du dépôt n’avait été prise et m’a indiqué être surprise qu’un colis d’une telle valeur ait été distribué sans signature, sans code de vérification et sans contrôle d’identité.

Malgré cela, AliExpress continue de considérer le simple statut « livré » comme suffisant, sans être en mesure de me fournir une preuve de remise à mon nom.

Je leur ai transmis une attestation sur l’honneur indiquant que je n’avais jamais reçu cette commande. J’ai également ouvert un litige auprès de PayPal et effectué toutes les démarches demandées. À ce jour, je n’ai toujours ni le produit, ni le remboursement.

Je considère avoir agi de bonne foi et avoir fourni tous les éléments en ma possession. J’attendais d’AliExpress qu’il protège ses clients lorsqu’une livraison d’un montant de 351,77 € est contestée. Au lieu de cela, j’ai le sentiment que la charge de la preuve repose entièrement sur l’acheteur, alors que le vendeur ne fournit pas de preuve de remise personnelle.

À défaut d’une solution, je poursuis désormais mes démarches auprès de ma protection juridique et des autorités compétentes.

J’espère sincèrement qu’AliExpress prendra enfin ses responsabilités et apportera une solution concrète à ce dossier.

review_text:
My Experience with AliExpress "Free Returns" – Buyer Beware

I have been an online shopper for many years and have used both AliExpress and Temu. Unfortunately, my recent experience with AliExpress has been extremely disappointing.

I specifically ordered a **blue bag** because I did not want a black one. The seller sent me what is clearly a **black bag**, not the colour I ordered.

Since the item I received did not match the listing, I requested a **free return and refund**, which AliExpress advertises on eligible products. The listing stated that it came with a **90-day Free Return** if the product did not meet expectations.

I submitted multiple return requests and provided photos showing the item I received. Each time, AliExpress rejected my request, saying my photos were "insufficient proof," despite the issue being that the product delivered did not match what I ordered.

What is most frustrating is that this isn't simply a case of changing my mind. I received an item that differs from what I purchased, yet I have still been unable to obtain the advertised free return.

In contrast, I have shopped with Temu for years and have had consistently straightforward experiences when using their free return policy. If an item is incorrect or doesn't meet expectations, the return process has been simple and hassle-free.

Based on my experience, I no longer have confidence in AliExpress's advertised Free Return policy. If you are considering buying from AliExpress because you believe the Free Return promise will protect you, I encourage you to carefully consider the potential difficulties if something goes wrong.

I hope AliExpress improves its dispute resolution process so that customers who receive items that do not match their orders can resolve the issue fairly and without unnecessary frustration.

This review reflects my personal experience with AliExpress and is intended to help other shoppers make informed purchasing decisions.

review_title: Fake Sterling Silver Jewlery Almost Got Arrested For Aliexpress Incompitence Leaving Seller Sell Fake Products
review_text:
I am writing this review to warn other consumers about my experience with AliExpress.

I purchased a chain advertised as 925 Sterling Silver for approximately €85. I also paid import VAT and customs charges when it entered Cyprus because I believed I was purchasing genuine sterling silver jewellery.

When I later took the chain to a professional jeweller and pawnbroker, I was informed that the item was not genuine 925 sterling silver and had no precious metal value. The situation became so serious that the police were called because jewellery falsely represented as precious metal raises obvious concerns. After I explained that I had bought it from AliExpress believing it was genuine, I was allowed to leave without any action being taken against me.

From that moment, I expected AliExpress to protect its customer. Instead, I received generic responses, was told about buyer protection time limits, and was even asked to upload evidence to Google Drive rather than having the item professionally examined.

I have repeatedly asked AliExpress and the seller to:

Provide proof that the chain is genuine 925 sterling silver.
Produce any certificate of authenticity or assay report supporting the "925" claim.
Arrange and pay for tracked shipping so the chain can be sent to AliExpress headquarters or an independent laboratory for testing.
Refund my purchase, reimburse my import costs, and take responsibility if the item is proven not to be sterling silver.

Instead of answering these requests directly, my case has simply been passed between departments. It is now being investigated under Case No. 2053808477177295.

In my opinion, this experience demonstrates a serious failure of consumer protection. A marketplace that allows products to be advertised as precious metal should be able to verify those claims when challenged.

I trusted AliExpress, paid approximately €85 for what was advertised as genuine sterling silver, and ended up with an item that, according to the professional who examined it, is not sterling silver.

Until AliExpress either proves the authenticity of the product or fully compensates me, I cannot recommend buying jewellery or precious metals through this platform.

I will update this review once AliExpress reaches a final decision.
